parameter_set.name: Balanced target
parameter_set.why: The template's GC content is in the ordinary range, so the published windows apply as stated.

provenance.note: Primer3 is bundled with primer3-py rather than installed separately, so its version is that package's.

reaction.note: Isothermal Bst-family LAMP design context at about 65 °C; this is a computation/protocol handoff, not evidence of observed amplification.

sets.note: 199 bases from the 5' end of F3 to the 3' end of B3c, with 2 of the two optional loop primers. Every oligo melts within 5.0 °C of every other, which is what one held temperature has to serve.

oligos.name: F3
oligos.note: Displaces the strand that FIP started, releasing the loop.

anneals.note: The half that binds the template melts at 60.9 °C. The whole oligo's 79.9 °C describes a molecule that does not exist until the reaction has run — half of it is a tail with nothing to bind yet.

oligos.name: FIP
oligos.note: Its F2 half anneals to the template; its F1c half is a 5' tail that is not on the template at all and becomes a primer later, folding back against the F1 copy on the strand this one makes.

anneals.note: The half that binds the template melts at 60.8 °C. The whole oligo's 81.1 °C describes a molecule that does not exist until the reaction has run — half of it is a tail with nothing to bind yet.

oligos.name: BIP
oligos.note: The same shape as FIP from the other end: the B2 half anneals, and the B1c half is the tail that closes the loop later.

oligos.name: B3
oligos.note: Displaces the strand that BIP started.

oligos.name: LF
oligos.note: Optional, and worth having: it primes inside the forward loop, which roughly halves the time to a result. It sits strictly between F2 and F1 — overlapping either would make it a perfect dimer with FIP.

oligos.name: LB
oligos.note: The backward loop's primer. It carries the plus-strand sequence rather than its complement, because the loop BIP makes is the other way round from the one FIP makes.
